label: input token v at the first or second position
explanation: Fires only in the original phase when the input token is v at step 0 or 1 (precision 1.0 on dev). Strength depends on position: v at t=1 is strongest (top activations ~0.87, e.g. after a leading y), and v at t=0 is moderate (~0.42). Some v inputs at t=2 also fire weakly (~0.07) and account for the ~5% of activations the predicate misses, about 1% of mass. Does not fire on v at t>=3, on any other token, or at the delimiter or during the copy phase (including when v is output or fed back).

issues: The claims hold up. On the test split the predicate (in_tok==v)&(t<=1) has precision 1.0, recall 0.953 and mass recall 0.99, with 0 false positives. v at t=0 and v at t=1 each fire every time (precision 1.0 each). t=1 carries about 60% of the activation mass and the top activations (0.872) are 'y v ...', so the magnitude claims match.
The feature fires only in the original phase. The delimiter and copy phase show 0 active steps, and t>=3 shows 0 active steps. The only active input token is v.

The misses are one consistent group: 1644 test steps, all v at t=2, firing weakly (up to about 0.2 relative to the max) and holding 1.0% of the activation mass. Only about 10% of v inputs at t=2 fire (precision 0.099), and adding t=2 lowers F1 to 0.825 (precision 0.70). The prev2_tok breakdown hints that firing at t=2 is somewhat more common after a leading j or p. That residue is too small to change the label.

Minor wording point: the explanation gives the t=2 activations as 'about 0.07', which is an absolute magnitude. Relative to the max they reach up to about 0.2, so it slightly understates them, but this is immaterial.
